pr_title: Bluetooth: Audio: Serialize subscription after discovery
pr_body:
The media control client used to subscribe to GMCS characteristics as
the characteristics were discovered, in effect queuing ATT requests.

Since then, the ATT MTU exchange has become automatic, leading to
larger ATT MTUs and more discovered characteristics per ATT response,
which again lead to the client enqueuing more subscriptions and
running out of buffers, with discovery failing as a result.

This PR moves the subscription to GMCS characteristics to a separate
sequence, so that it happens serially after discovery, rather than in 
parallel with the discovery.

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/44579

issue_context.title: MCC: Discovery cannot complete with success
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
The Client fails to complete MCS and OTS discovery. The discovery is aborted in the middle due to lack of resources in ATT (to store the `bt_att_req`) and the discovery is aborted after 30 seconds of ATT Timeout (see `req = bt_att_req_alloc(BT_ATT_TIMEOUT);` in `gatt_req_alloc`).

The Media Control Client discovery implementation is not efficient in terms of CCC subscription. The `CONFIG_BT_GATT_AUTO_DISCOVER_CCC` is enabled, so the `ATT: Find Information Request` is used to find CCC's.
The implementation sends bunch of `ATT: Find Information Request` to find a CCC for a given characteristic. Each `ATT: Find Information Response` contains multiple Handle-UUID pairs that could be used to find CCC of multiple characteristics, but are discarded instead. 

I'm not sure whether it's MCC implementation only bug or rather `CONFIG_BT_GATT_AUTO_DISCOVER_CCC` feature that could be more efficient or used differently to be more efficient.

**To Reproduce**
* Use shell with audio.conf `west build -b native_posix  ~/zephyrproject/zephyr/tests/bluetooth/shell/ --pristine -- -DOVERLAY_CONFIG=audio.conf`
* `mcc init`
* Connect to MCS device
* `mcc discover_mcs`

**Expected behavior**
Discovery completes with no error.

comments:
I think the `CONFIG_BT_GATT_AUTO_DISCOVER_CCC` discussion is better fitted for a different issue. `CONFIG_BT_GATT_AUTO_DISCOVER_CCC` will only find a single CCCD, and it will do a discovery for each CCC to subscribe to (of which there are many in MCS). There is room for improvement there, but it isn't any different than us doing `bt_gatt_discover` for each service instead of a single `bt_gatt_discover` for multiple services (assuming that the MTU supports that). 

@MariuszSkamra Was this run with the `/tests/bluetooth/shell/`? 
One thing we haven't considered is that the number of TX buffers required in many of the implementations will increase by the MTU: If the entire MCS service is returned in a single read, then we will likely attempt to subscribe to all the CCCs based on that single read. If the MTU is large (such as 64 in this case), then we should actually probably be able to do a single write to multiple CCCDs. 

The alternative is of course to adapt the less (time) efficient approach of doing
1. Discover service
2. Discover specific characteristic
3. [Optionally] subscribe to specific characteristic
4. Repeat 2 and 3 until entire service characteristic range is discovered

This approach will require less memory as we never need more than a single discover parameter, but it will likewise also increase the number of GATT operations to be performed for discovery. IIRC this is approach of the HAS client, right @MariuszSkamra ?

@Thalley Yes, `/tests/bluetooth/shell/` was used.
@Thalley Indeed, this approach is used in HAS client, but I think more efficient way to do this is such a big service like this is:

1. Discover service
2. Discover all characteristics within service range and store handles.
3. Once the characteristic discovery is complete, subscribe to.

But still there is a possibility that some of the information might be lost in `ATT: Find Information Response`. when `bt_gatt_subscribe` is used with `CONFIG_BT_GATT_AUTO_DISCOVER_CCC` option enabled. 

As the solution  I would suggest using `bt_gatt_discover` with type `BT_GATT_DISCOVER_ATTRIBUTE` and handle range <service start handle, service end handle> to find all of the attributes within range. By doing that one gets all of the characteristic value handles + all of the descriptors. So,

1. Discover service
2. Discover attributes (as the result we get characteristic value handles and CCCD handles) (use `ATT: Find Information Request`)
3. Subscribe to

Indeed, that will be more efficient. 

The `CONFIG_BT_GATT_AUTO_DISCOVER_CCC` was defined to be an easy way of doing it, not an efficient way :D 

It will require additional effect for the service client implementation to match the CCID handles with characteristic handles, but will certainly be an optimization (in both air time and memory).

The issue seems to be somehow related to the ATT MTU size or the ATT MTU exchange.

The discovery shell command started failing after commit 6eafc64855192fba71b43a95ce85f12c3d5e1b24  Bluetooth: audio: Enable auto ATT MTU Exchange for BASS and unicast client

For the commit before this the discovery command succeeds.  But it fails if "gatt exchange-mtu" is done before the discovery.

The BabbleSim test for mcc does not fail, however, even though that also does the ATT AUTO MTU exchange.

> The issue seems to be somehow related to the ATT MTU size or the ATT MTU exchange.
> 
> The discovery shell command started failing after commit [6eafc64](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/6eafc64855192fba71b43a95ce85f12c3d5e1b24) Bluetooth: audio: Enable auto ATT MTU Exchange for BASS and unicast client
> 
> For the commit before this the discovery command succeeds. But it fails if "gatt exchange-mtu" is done before the discovery.
> 
> The BabbleSim test for mcc does not fail, however, even though that also does the ATT AUTO MTU exchange.

Correct. 

With a larger MTU, we get more characteristics in a single discovery GATT command response, thus triggering more subscribe requests while handling the discovery response. 

The quick workaround for this is to increase the number of TX buffers to the number of characteristics we'll subscribe to (expensive, and will still cause issues if e.g. doing any other discovery procedure or GATT procedure).

The proper workaround is to do these subscribe requests _after_ discovery as suggested by @MariuszSkamra, which would keep the number of buffers to a minimum, but will require additional handling in the MCC.

review_comments: Could it be an issue that`discover_params` are global (not per mcs instance?). What happens when connected to 2 devices in coordinated set?
The MCC does not yet support multiple connections (at all), but it would still make sense to move `discover_params` and `read_params` to the `struct mcs_instance_t`

I had a go at this.  The issue with it is that the MCS instance is not assigned until after an MCS service has been discovered.  (Which makes sense, I think.)  So that creates a chicken-and-egg problem - no discovery parameters until the service has been discovered.
While I agree that this is something that can be improved, I would like to postpone that to get this bugfix itself in.
Created https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/47335 for the issue.
Not related to this change, but you could save 32 bytes (16 characteristics * 2bytes per handle) if you could reuse `value_handle` stored in `bt_gatt_subscribe_params`

I am not sure I follow.
The pointer to the discovery params can not be reused, as that is used as a persistent flag.
(This is anyway outside the scope of this PR, so I would like to take this as a separate issue.)

I think that his point is that `playback_speed_handle` is the same value as `playback_speed_sub_params.value_handle`, so we are basically duplicating that value for each characteristic we have a `struct bt_gatt_subscribe_params` for. 

I think this is outside the scope of this PR, and a general optimization we can have in LE Audio.
